It's November 7, 2026, and this is AI Tech News. OpenAI has reportedly raised another 11 billion dollars at a 1.25 trillion dollar valuation, according to Bloomberg, in a round expected to close in the coming weeks. That comes not long after it raised 122 billion dollars in March at an 852 billion dollar valuation. Politics is shaking the industry. In this week's U.S. midterms, voters weighed in on 41 data center ballot measures, and in all but one, the majority backed more restrictions. Meta warned the backlash could make AI expansion harder, and OpenAI said it will stop using non-disclosure agreements with public officials on data center projects. Meanwhile, Ramp data shows AI usage still climbing but spending stalling, as price cuts and cost controls take hold, just as Anthropic nears its IPO. The New York Times reports China's intelligence agency recruited Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, seeking information on American AI chips. And Meta introduced Spaces in its Muse AI, letting the assistant build custom, app-like experiences such as shopping hubs, school dashboards, and trivia games. That's all for today's AI Tech News.

After this week's midterms, where voters across party lines opposed data center expansion, OpenAI announced new community commitments, including no longer using non-disclosure agreements with public officials. Users can connect bank and card accounts through Plaid and ask questions like where their money went this month. That's AI Tech News for today. Thanks for listening.
